symptom: Distinct caller-owned JavaScript strings containing an unpaired UTF-16 surrogate and U+FFFD produced identical UTF-8 byte sequences before SHA-256 transcript hashing. The exported standalone request digest could therefore assign the same correlation digest to different untrusted metadata without a cryptographic hash collision. This was reproduced with synthetic Node.js inputs only; no independent authority, production or private data was involved.
lesson: SHA-256 cannot distinguish different JavaScript strings if the UTF-8 encoder first replaces malformed UTF-16 with identical U+FFFD bytes. Reject unpaired surrogate code units at the standalone request transcript boundary; preserve valid surrogate pairs and unchanged valid transcript bytes.
guardrail: Before length-prefixing and UTF-8 hashing each untrusted request metadata string, reject isolated high or low UTF-16 surrogates with INVALID_UNTRUSTED_REQUEST. Regression-test high-surrogate versus replacement-character byte alias, a low-surrogate settlement field, a malformed revision identifier, a valid surrogate pair and unchanged well-formed transcript digests. The digest remains an untrusted correlation ID, not evidence authentication or scoring authority.
